evidence: The Charmels, signed to Stax's Volt subsidiary, recorded 'As Long as I've Got You' (1967), written for them by staff songwriters Isaac Hayes and David Porter, the same in-house writing team behind much of Sam & Dave's catalogue, as documented in Stax's own history.

later.title: As Long as I've Got You

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Both records come from the same writing room: Hayes and Porter's melodic instinct and a horn-driven Stax arrangement. Sam & Dave's version is a full-band, up-tempo declaration; the Charmels', a year later, slows the same songwriting team's sensibility into a sadder, sparer piano ballad, the version a producer would later go looking for.

explanation.age7: Two songwriters who worked for the Stax record label wrote a sad, pretty song for the Charmels, a girl group nobody remembered until a rap producer found it years later.
explanation.age13: Stax's staff songwriters Isaac Hayes and David Porter, already known for writing hits for Sam & Dave, wrote 'As Long as I've Got You' for the Charmels in 1967. It went nowhere commercially at the time, one of many records the label's in-house writing system produced.
explanation.adult: A scene-to-artist edge naming the mechanism this map's other Stax and Motown edges also describe: an in-house writing and production system, not a single artist's own creative choices, is what put this specific song into existence at all.
